profiles.meeting_scenario: A planning meeting for a 6-week ML research sprint to turn an internal prototype on physics-informed wireless channel modeling into a workshop submission and reproducible demo. The team wants to extend a prior indoor channel-prediction case study that combines semantic segmentation with deep learning, framing it as a more generalizable PINN-style pipeline for indoor mmWave propagation. The agenda is to decide the exact scope of the study, what experiments and artifacts need to be produced, who owns each part of the pipeline, and what must be ready for an internal checkpoint in two weeks. The expected outcome is a shared plan covering experiment setup, deliverables for the checkpoint, responsibilities, and a tentative submission timeline.

members.name: Dr. Lena Hoffmann
members.expertise: Physics-informed neural networks, wireless propagation modeling, experimental design for ML papers
members.background: Lena leads a small academic-industry collaboration on data-driven channel modeling and previously co-authored an indoor mmWave study using semantic maps and learned propagation predictors.
members.private_state: She wants a tightly scoped, submission-ready story that can show progress quickly without reopening infrastructure work, and she is trying to reuse as much of the prior prototype and prior evaluation conventions as possible.
hidden_assumptions: When the team says 'the indoor case study,' it naturally refers to the office-wing environment used in the main figures of the prior internal draft, not every indoor scene the lab has touched.
The phrase 'segmentation pipeline' refers to the manually cleaned semantic masks produced for the February pilot, because those are the only masks she considers stable enough for a paper timeline.
A 'generalization check' for this sprint means showing transfer to unseen transmitter-receiver placements within the same building geometry, since cross-building transfer would be a next-stage claim.
For an 'overnight sweep,' the sensible default is to fine-tune from the existing pretrained propagation backbone using the lab's fixed launch script and standard seed set.

members.name: Arjun Mehta
members.expertise: Scene understanding, semantic segmentation pipelines, reproducible training infrastructure for wireless ML
members.background: Arjun has been maintaining the lab's newer indoor data-processing stack, including an automated floor-plan-to-semantics parser and experiment orchestration scripts for multi-scene training.
members.private_state: He wants the project to demonstrate real cross-layout robustness and to showcase the newer automated pipeline, which he sees as the most publishable and scalable contribution for his dissertation.
hidden_assumptions: When people mention 'the indoor case study,' they mean the broader indoor benchmark bundle assembled over the summer, including office, lab, and lobby scenes, because that is the current lab dataset package.
The phrase 'segmentation pipeline' refers to the newer automated parser that generates semantic masks from floor plans and LiDAR alignment, since that is what he now uses by default.
A 'generalization check' should mean evaluating on an unseen building or floor layout; otherwise the term generalizable would feel overstated in a paper about wireless channel modeling.
An 'overnight sweep' normally means full reruns from scratch through the shared Slurm template so the results are cleanly reproducible end to end.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the indoor case study
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to 'extend the indoor case study.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the original office-wing indoor environment at 28 GHz with the same geometry family as the prior prototype, adding only limited extra runs.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the full summer indoor bundle spanning office, lab, and lobby scenes, because that is the current internal benchmark package.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both have recently worked on indoor channel prediction and both use the same shorthand, so the phrase sounds fully settled; neither sees any need to restate scene boundaries during a planning meeting.

misalignment_points.topic: Which segmentation pipeline is 'the existing one'
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to 'reuse the existing segmentation pipeline.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is referring to the manually corrected semantic masks from the February pilot that were used to produce the prior internal figures.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is referring to the automated floor-plan/LiDAR parser he finished in June and now considers the lab's default segmentation stack.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both pipelines already exist and both have been described informally as 'the segmentation pipeline,' so the reference feels unambiguous from each person's perspective even though they mean different artifacts.

misalignment_points.topic: What qualifies as a generalization result
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree the paper needs a 'generalization check.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes this is satisfied by holding out receiver grids and transmitter placements within the same building while showing stable error and physically plausible trends.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes this requires at least one unseen building or floor layout so the model demonstrates transfer across distinct scene geometries.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The shared goal word 'generalization' carries positive consensus and neither person expects disagreement about the standard behind it, especially because no one is debating the headline claim directly.

misalignment_points.topic: How the overnight sweep will be run
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to 'do the overnight sweep before the checkpoint.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes Arjun will fine-tune from the current pretrained propagation backbone using the lab's fixed seeds on the reserved four-GPU node, mainly to get fast comparative numbers.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes he will launch clean end-to-end reruns from scratch through the shared cluster template so the pipeline is fully reproducible across scenes.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The sweep is framed as routine execution rather than a design choice, and both approaches are common in the lab, so each hears the phrase as a straightforward operational step rather than something needing clarification.
